original.title: Firm Resources and Sustained Competitive Advantage

core_idea: Firms differ in the resources they control, and those differences persist. A resource can be a source of sustained competitive advantage if it is valuable, rare, hard to imitate and non-substitutable (the VRIN criteria). Strategy should therefore start from what the firm has, not only from the industry it is in.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: Why do some firms outperform others in the same industry?
Which resources or capabilities explain a firm's or sector's advantage (e.g. in SMEs, family firms, startups)?
Typical data: firm surveys, financial data, case studies of resources and capabilities.
common_mistakes: Calling any asset a 'resource' without showing it meets the VRIN criteria.
Arguing in a circle: the resource is valuable because the firm succeeded.
Ignoring how resources are built and changed over time (see dynamic capabilities).
